messages.text: Will a power spike fry the whole miner?

Great question — and this is actually one of the Rev 6.1's standout design choices.

**No — a power spike hits the F1 fuse first, not your miner.**

Here's how it works:

- The board has an **onboard F1 fuse** (a small automotive-style blade fuse, right next to the yellow XT30 power input)
- If a spike hits, **F1 sacrifices itself** — the electronics behind it stay protected
- Cheaper miners skip this entirely — a spike there cooks the whole board

**The X.30 connector helps too:**
- Rev 5 used an 8 A barrel jack that would sag and melt under load
- Rev 6.1 swaps in a **keyed 15 A XT30** — no brown-outs, no cooked connector at full 6 TH/s draw

Bottom line: worst case, you replace a cheap fuse — not a $249 miner. That's the design intent.
Is it quiet enough to run in my office?

Yes, comfortably.

- **~40–45 dB** — roughly quiet-room / library level
- **0.5 kg, ~20 cm** — palm-sized, sits on its included 3D-printed stand
- One large front fan moving air slowly = no high-pitched whine

At full 6 TH/s it runs **~57 °C on the ASICs** — cool enough to sustain 24/7 without the fan ever needing to scream.

Drop it to eco mode (~4.8 TH/s / ~71 W) and it gets even quieter and cooler.

**Short answer:** desk, bookshelf, home office — it's built for exactly that.
